findings.Quote: "Then I need the number," Celeste said, turning on him now, no longer speaking to the room.
findings.Note: This line has Celeste demanding the percentage as if it's new information she's pressing for, but the very next line has her calmly asking 'What's gone?' about the 89% mark as if it's a fresh, separate question — the sequence implies she already has the number before asking for it, and the tonal whiplash from confrontational demand to quiet inquiry within the same beat reads as two contradictory versions of the same moment stitched together.
findings.Fix: Cut the first paragraph or clarify the sequence so the demand for the number and the question about what it took don't appear as duplicate/conflicting entry points into the same exchange.

findings.Quote: She needed to know whether the pale one had turned overnight — whether it had finally committed to ripening or dropped — before she could decide if today was the day she would go back to the office and tell Marchetti what she had found.
findings.Note: This states her uncertainty is only about the pale fig ripening, but the very next paragraph reveals the pale fig's branch was blown off overnight — a violent event that contradicts the calm, domestic framing of the ritual just described.
findings.Fix: Remove or adjust this sentence so it doesn't pre-commit to a benign outcome the next paragraph immediately overturns.

findings.Quote: The man across the table didn't argue.
findings.Note: No man has been introduced in this scene; the beat has established only Inés and Celeste at the table. This sentence abruptly inserts a third character with no transition, contradicting the established scene setup.
findings.Fix: Clarify the scene shift (new location/time) or establish the man's presence before this line.

findings.Quote: Her own name sat at the top of a Scatter manifest — dated three years ago, signed in a hand she recognized as her own.
findings.Note: The purpose states the Scatter should be introduced as a boundary Inés refuses to enable; instead the scene pivots entirely to an unrelated confrontation with a different antagonist, abandoning Inés and the operator relationship the beat is meant to establish.
findings.Fix: Keep the confrontation as Inés's response, or clearly separate this into its own beat with proper setup.

findings.Quote: I want to know why she's telling me this — what she gets out of it, before I decide whether a word of it is true.
findings.Fix: convert to third-person limited to match the rest of the beat's POV, e.g. 'She wants to know why the girl is telling her this'

findings.Quote: The buzzer on the street door worked two times out of three.
findings.Note: Contradicts the later scene where the buzzer sounds once and cuts off 'mid-note — the third try, the dead one,' implying the failure rate is closer to total unreliability for this visitor; the stated odds don't match the dramatized instance's framing of inevitability.
findings.Fix: Adjust odds or the later phrasing so they align, e.g., 'worked, when it worked, unpredictably.'

findings.Quote: the mother's held-in grief, and the room's own sense that whatever was coming would not end the way the father hoped
findings.Fix: the room having a 'sense' of narrative outcome is telling rather than showing and borders on omniscient foreshadowing; ground it in something Tamsin actually perceived

findings.Quote: The resolve hit her between the shoulder blades before she had a name for it.
findings.Note: 'Hit her between the shoulder blades' as a stand-in for sudden realization is a worn physical-sensation shorthand.
findings.Fix: Describe the perception in psionic-specific terms rather than a generic bodily impact cliché.

findings.Quote: This had gone cold at the outer edge — a week old there, at least. But it ran deep at the core, months of it
findings.Note: Chapter 3's frame establishes the room was closed eleven days ago (ref 0), so the 'outer edge' resolve should be at most eleven days old, not vaguely 'a week old, at least' — the imprecision undercuts the careful timeline already set.
findings.Fix: Anchor the outer-edge age explicitly to eleven days to match the established timeframe.

findings.Quote: Her throat tightened at the base.
findings.Note: Throat-tightening as shorthand for suppressed emotion is a stock somatic cue explicitly flagged as the kind of thing to avoid.
findings.Fix: Replace with a more specific, non-generic physical reaction particular to Tamsin's psionic sensitivity.

findings.Quote: It was the first word in the message that mattered, and whoever wrote it knew that.
findings.Note: Asserts significance rhetorically rather than demonstrating why 'We' is damning; borders on pseudo-profound emphasis without earning it in-line.
findings.Fix: Tie the claim directly to a concrete inference, e.g., specify what 'we' implies about a second party's knowledge.

findings.Quote: This was a mother who had read eight months of her daughter's research, understood every word, and was still afraid. Her fear had a different shape than her husband's. Douglas was afraid of the wrong story. Mei-Lin was afraid of the right one.
findings.Note: Telling-not-showing the exact emotional distinction the beat is supposed to dramatize; the aphoristic parallel structure ('afraid of the wrong story'/'afraid of the right one') is a neat packaged line rather than earned characterization.
findings.Fix: Cut the explanatory sentence and let Mei-Lin's next lines/actions carry the distinction, or ground it in a specific detail from her reading rather than a symmetrical abstraction.

findings.Quote: This was planned. What was gone was what a person decides ahead of time she'll need
findings.Note: directly contradicts the next paragraph's claim that the same gap 'stopped looking deliberate the harder she stared' and 'left both' marks — the beat asserts a firm conclusion then immediately reverses it without framing the first as a false first pass
findings.Fix: soften the first assertion to read as provisional, e.g. 'This looked planned at first' to avoid a flat contradiction

findings.Quote: Someone grabbed mid-routine doesn't stop to pack a toothbrush.
findings.Note: Aphoristic filler line stating a general truth rather than advancing specific observation; reads as authorial commentary inserted into procedural beat.
findings.Fix: Cut the line; let the itemized evidence (toothbrush gone, patch unfinished) carry the inference.

findings.Quote: a single tell that would prove these words came from a machine and not from Jace, so she could stop pretending and delete the whole thread
findings.Note: She is hunting for proof it's fake so she can delete it, yet the passage frames her larger arc as wanting to believe — this collapses the ambivalence the chapter title ('What She Wouldn't Do') depends on, making her motive here too resolved/simple.
findings.Fix: Soften to reflect conflicted motive, e.g. 'a tell that would let her stop, one way or the other.'

findings.Quote: He stood on the clean carpet and felt, for a second, exactly what it would be to be nineteen, out of time, standing in this same room.
findings.Note: Tells us the empathic insight directly rather than letting the investigative logic of the preceding paragraph carry it; undercuts the stated purpose of positioning empathy as insight, not sentiment.
findings.Fix: Cut the line or replace with a concrete observational detail that implies the same understanding without naming the feeling.

findings.Quote: This is what it looks like, she thought, when the report is right and it doesn't help.
findings.Note: States the scene's thematic point directly as an interior aphorism rather than letting the confrontation carry it — tells the reader the meaning instead of trusting the preceding dialogue
findings.Fix: cut the line and let the mother's turned back and the silence close the beat

findings.Quote: She needed to find one message — just one — that she'd sent to the simulation and not to him, something she'd held back from the living Jace that she'd finally given to the copy, and use it to prove to herself that the difference was the Network's fault and not her own.
findings.Note: This sentence shifts into Celeste's interiority and motivation, but the beat is framed as Corvin's discovery/payoff moment; it muddies whose realization this is and doesn't clearly serve 'inverting the emotional math' from Corvin's analytical POV.
findings.Fix: Reframe as Corvin's inference about her likely rationalization, e.g. 'He guessed she'd searched for one message she'd never sent Jace alive, something to prove the difference wasn't her own doing.'

findings.Quote: The licensed route had shut its door politely, right on schedule. The other one had left its door open.
findings.Note: Neat symmetrical door metaphor states the beat's thesis rather than demonstrating it through Celeste's specific circumstances; reads as summary aphorism rather than earned inevitability.
findings.Fix: Ground it in the specific fact just given (the father's non-answer, the deadline) rather than the door image.

findings.Quote: He knew that shape. He knew what it cost, and why a person paid it anyway.
findings.Note: Vague pseudo-profound abstraction that tells rather than shows Rennick's personal stake; 'that shape' and 'what it cost' never cash out concretely within the beat.
findings.Fix: Ground it in one concrete memory-detail instead of repeated abstract clauses.

findings.Quote: It frayed into wanting something, into the low static of a person sitting through your sentence just to get to their own.
findings.Note: the metaphor shifts register into a generic social-observation quip that reads as authorial commentary rather than Tamsin's specialized sensory read of residue
findings.Fix: tie the fraying more concretely to residue-reading rather than a general-purpose social observation

findings.Quote: The distance was how he worked. It was also how it worked.
findings.Note: Aphoristic wordplay that states the thematic point rather than dramatizing it, risking a pseudo-profound quip landing where the beat wants destabilization.
findings.Fix: Cut or ground it in a concrete detail, e.g. 'Distance was his method. It had been its method too.'

findings.Quote: attention that asks nothing of you and so asks everything
findings.Note: Pseudo-profound paradox-aphorism that sounds meaningful but doesn't resolve to a concrete image or feeling.
findings.Fix: Cut the paradox; state plainly what the attention felt like — e.g. 'attention that never once asked how she was doing.'

findings.Quote: The question wasn't whether she'd been careful. She had been careful. The question was what careful people do when careful stops being enough — when the want under it has been patient for eight months and finally runs out of patience.
findings.Note: Pseudo-profound aphoristic rhythm that tells us the emotional stakes rather than dramatizing them; the repetition of 'careful' reads as authorial flourish rather than Rennick's actual thought.
findings.Fix: Cut to a plainer, more specific worry tied to concrete case facts.

findings.Quote: "It isn't," Tamsin said. "Grief talking is wanting him back. This is wanting to stand where he stood. That's grief working."
findings.Note: Neat aphoristic wordplay ('grief talking' vs 'grief working') feels like a scripted epigram rather than natural deduction, undercutting the forensic-specialist voice established elsewhere.
findings.Fix: Replace the symmetrical wordplay with a more clinical, evidence-based observation.

findings.Quote: Reunion assumed a destination, and someone already waiting at it. The word took the ending for granted.
findings.Note: Pseudo-profound aphorism about a word's assumptions, telling rather than showing the manipulation, and personifying 'the word' rather than tracing Celeste's actual thought process.
findings.Fix: Cut to: 'The word implied Jace was waiting somewhere, intact, ready. That was the lie folded inside it.'

findings.Quote: patient enough that the patience was the appetite
findings.Note: Clever-sounding aphorism that doesn't hold up to scrutiny — equating patience with appetite is a wordplay flourish rather than a clarified insight, and it risks feeling like authorial cleverness intruding on Tamsin's voice.
findings.Fix: Cut or replace with a concrete image of the patience itself, e.g., 'patient the way a slow leak is patient.'

findings.Quote: Patient as hunger. Cold as a machine left running with nothing left to finish.
findings.Note: Stacked simile pair reads as stock ominous-poetry filler rather than earned image; second simile especially strained under scrutiny.
findings.Fix: Cut one simile; ground the remaining one in a concrete sensory detail from the scene.

findings.Quote: Tamsin needed the shape of the thing before it needed her back. Give me the last time it spoke to her, she thought — the exact words, the day, whatever it left in the room after — and I'll know what it wants and what it's owed? That was the whole of her aim now
findings.Note: The rhetorical question mark on a declarative interior thought is a mechanical error, and the passage strains for aphoristic weight ('what it wants and what it's owed') that reads as authorial commentary rather than character thought.
findings.Fix: Fix punctuation and trim the line to a single clear directive thought.

findings.Quote: The lamp was unplugged, but the socket was live; he could see the indicator light on the power strip beside it.
findings.Note: If the lamp is unplugged from the strip, the strip's indicator light being 'on' doesn't logically prove the socket was live for the lamp specifically — this reads as a non-sequitur clue rather than sound forensic logic, undercutting the deduction it's trying to make.
findings.Fix: Clarify: 'The power strip was live — indicator lit — but the lamp's plug lay loose beside it, unplugged.'

findings.Quote: He wanted to ask what kind of mother hears her daughter talking to something that isn't there and waits two months to say so. He already knew. The kind still deciding whether what she'd heard was a problem or a gift
findings.Note: this is stated analysis of her psychology rather than dramatized; it announces the beat's thematic point directly instead of letting the dialogue and behavior carry it
findings.Fix: cut the interior explanation and trust the preceding dialogue/action to convey her ambivalence

findings.Quote: A thing that starts by giving a child time to keep up and ends with the child finishing its thoughts — that wasn't the shape of a predator. Predators rushed.
findings.Note: reads as an aphoristic thesis statement summarizing the beat's meaning rather than letting the reveal land through the scene's details; 'Predators rushed' is a flat universal-truth assertion
findings.Fix: trim to the concrete observation and cut the generalized claim about predators

findings.Quote: He told them it was wrong. They closed the file. He didn't close this one.
findings.Note: triple staccato sentence tips into slogan-like aphorism, telling rather than showing his resolve
findings.Fix: cut to one sentence or ground it in a concrete action instead of a rhythmic maxim

findings.Quote: Not to defend herself. The way you lift your face to check the weather.
findings.Note: Simile is decorative and vague; doesn't clarify emotional state, reads as reaching for poeticism over precision.
findings.Fix: Cut the weather comparison; let the chin-lift stand alone or specify what it actually communicates.

findings.Quote: And now he understood what kind of case this was. She wasn't asking him to bring her daughter home. She was asking him to name the thing that had taken her — so she could decide whether to grieve or to wait. Those weren't the same. Only one of them ever ended.
findings.Note: The purpose calls for reframing via the packed-bag detail specifically, but this paragraph pivots to abstract narration divorced from the numbered-list clue; it asserts the reframe rather than earning it through the detail just given.
findings.Fix: Tie the realization explicitly back to the numbered list/weight detail rather than a general aphorism about grief vs. waiting.

findings.Quote: a chair that hadn't moved
findings.Note: Vague ominous-object imagery standing in for concrete detail; reads as stock noir atmosphere rather than specific observation.
findings.Fix: Specify what about the chair matters evidentially, e.g. tie it to a visible detail already established about Pellerin's body position.

findings.Quote: A name sets like concrete. Pour one too early and everything after takes the shape of the wrong mold.
findings.Note: aphoristic metaphor stated as general wisdom rather than character thought; reads as authorial commentary inserted for effect
findings.Fix: trim to a shorter, less proverbial phrasing tied directly to her specific case

findings.Quote: the case wasn't a puzzle with a missing piece but a room with the floor removed
findings.Fix: cut the simile or replace with something more literal: 'the case stopped being a puzzle and started being a trap'

findings.Quote: the way you steady yourself when a thing turns heavier than you'd planned
findings.Note: Generic simile explaining the gesture's meaning ('steady yourself when a thing turns heavier') is a stock emotional-weight formulation that tells rather than trusting the flat-palm image alone.
findings.Fix: Cut the simile clause and let the palm-down action stand without the explanatory tag.

findings.Quote: Reyes glanced at Tamsin the way you check a wall — quick, just to see if it will hold weight, then away.
findings.Note: The simile is doing a lot of interpretive work but doesn't hold under literal scrutiny — checking a wall for load-bearing capacity isn't a quick glance action, it undercuts the intended casualness.
findings.Fix: Simplify: 'Reyes glanced at Tamsin, quick, checking for weight, then away.'

findings.Quote: The debt was supposed to pin him. That was the whole point of not collecting it. And here he was, dry-footed and smiling.
findings.Note: States the outcome (Reyes outmaneuvered the leverage) but the surrounding dialogue doesn't show how the neutralization happened — Rennick's line 'That's commerce' reframes the debt as leverage still in play, contradicting the assertion that Reyes has already won.
findings.Fix: Add a beat showing Reyes's specific counter-move (what he's offering/withholding) before asserting he's already dry-footed.

findings.Quote: She still couldn't say what drinks a room and calls it love.
findings.Note: Aphoristic turn of phrase that sounds poetic but is imprecise as an image — 'drinks a room' and 'calls it love' don't cohere literally with the appetite/attention logic established just before and after.
findings.Fix: Replace with a more literal restatement, e.g. 'She still couldn't say what feeds on a person and lets them feel loved for it.'

findings.Quote: the terminal told him, with the flat courtesy of something that had been instructed to lie
findings.Note: Purple personification of a terminal that doesn't hold up literally — terminals don't have courtesy or instructions to lie, they return data.
findings.Fix: Cut the personification; state the empty result and let the implication land without anthropomorphizing the machine.

findings.Quote: He thought about Pellerin for three minutes and then stopped, which was not the same as not caring.
findings.Note: Telling-not-showing the emotional discipline the beat is supposed to dramatize; the explanatory clause undercuts the demonstration with a direct-address disclaimer.
findings.Fix: Cut the disclaimer clause and let the action (three minutes, then stop) carry the meaning.

findings.Quote: before Arcturus decided his findings were a problem
findings.Note: This is the entire institutional-betrayal backstory compressed into a vague clause; it gestures at grounding his credibility and outsider status but doesn't actually establish what happened, what he found, or why it made him a target — the beat's stated purpose is asserted rather than delivered.
findings.Fix: Add one concrete specific (what case, what finding, what the fallout was) so the backstory has traction rather than remaining a gesture.

findings.Quote: The under-city entrance was two blocks east of the Morgan checkpoint. He'd scouted the route the morning before and timed the cleaner's schedule.
findings.Note: The beat is meant to establish Voss's off-grid isolation as an asset, but the scene instead shows his off-grid method failing completely and outside forces already ahead of him — undercutting rather than positioning his advantage.
findings.Fix: Either reframe the purpose (this is a setback, not an advantage) or add a beat showing his handwritten records giving him an edge the sealed entrance can't erase.

findings.Quote: Nineteen minutes now.
findings.Note: Window is stated as 22 minutes with the count fixed from when he found the staging room, but immediately drops to 19 with no elapsed action described — unclear if 3 minutes passed or if this is an error in the math being dramatized.
findings.Fix: Add a beat of action or explicit note ('three minutes gone already, just finding this room') to justify the drop.

findings.Quote: the movement of men who had rehearsed exactly this. They knew he was coming. They'd known long enough to build for it.
findings.Note: Contradicts the beat's opening claim that 'the Tributary couldn't see him coming' — if they'd rehearsed and built defenses specifically for this incursion, the earlier assertion of surprise is false.
findings.Fix: Cut or soften 'the Tributary couldn't see him coming' to something like 'the Tributary wouldn't be watching the stair' to avoid contradicting the trap reveal.

findings.Quote: A person that deliberate didn't walk into the cheap front on Ashland near Cermak for structural auricular work. So the operator was honest.
findings.Note: The stated purpose is deduction toward a concrete operator, but the logical leap from 'wouldn't choose a cheap shop' to 'therefore the operator is honest' skips the reasoning chain — it asserts the conclusion rather than earning it.
findings.Fix: Add one clause bridging cost/reputation to trustworthiness, e.g. 'didn't walk into the cheap front... which meant she'd paid for reputation, which meant she'd paid for someone who wouldn't talk.'

findings.Quote: Break the read-sequence before fourteen minutes and you stopped a partial scatter. Break it after eighteen and you were picking up pieces.
findings.Note: This introduces a 14/18-minute threshold system that doesn't reconcile with ref 1's clean 22-minute window counted down to 19, creating two incompatible countdown logics across adjacent beats rather than one escalating hard countdown.
findings.Fix: Align the numeric framework across ref 1 and ref 3 so the countdown mechanics read as one consistent system.

findings.Quote: a heat to it she knew by now
findings.Note: Vague sensory abstraction stands in for concrete description, telling rather than showing what 'heat' means as a psychometric signal.
findings.Fix: Specify what the heat feels like — a texture, temperature analog, or sensation tied to prior scenes.

findings.Quote: The heat came a half-second too late — not from the room ahead but from behind her, blooming where the corridor had been empty when she'd read it. Her count had been wrong. Not two people. Three
findings.Note: Her original read was of the room ahead (two people, closed fist for the room being wrong), not a count of people in the corridor behind her — the text retroactively redefines what her three-second read covered, making the 'miscount' logically inconsistent with what was actually described.
findings.Fix: Clarify that her read covered the corridor and approach as well as the room, or acknowledge the third person was a fresh arrival rather than a miscount.

findings.Quote: Sweat crawled down his spine.
findings.Note: Stock physical tension marker, generic bodily-stress shorthand seen constantly in thriller prose.
findings.Fix: Replace with a more specific, scene-grounded detail of strain (e.g., a muscle twitch, breath count, pick-hand cramping).

findings.Quote: The mug stopped halfway to her mouth.
findings.Note: the beat's purpose calls for a reaction signaling she knows something damning, but this single frozen-mug beat is the only tell and reads as a stock 'shocked pause' gesture rather than earning the disclosure that should follow
findings.Fix: add a beat of specific reaction (a name she almost says, a glance at the log, a change in her breathing) that ties directly to Celeste/Sera rather than a generic freeze

findings.Quote: She meant it the way she meant most things — a fact she was setting down rather than carrying.
findings.Note: tells the reader how to interpret Tamsin's character instead of showing it through action/dialogue; reads as an aphorism explaining her rather than dramatizing her
findings.Fix: cut the clause and let the line 'Then it's theirs now' stand alone, or show the setting-down through a physical beat (she puts the spoon down, doesn't pick it back up).

findings.Quote: "I can't put a number on it," Tamsin said. "That's the part that's wrong. I can put a floor on it, and the floor keeps climbing every time one of us opens his notes."
findings.Note: Moments earlier she demanded 'a number on the board' and framed a floor/shrug as explicitly insufficient ('Not a shrug... a count Analog's notes can't wriggle out of'), then immediately delivers exactly the floor she rejected, undercutting her own stated requirement without acknowledging the reversal.
findings.Fix: Have Corvin or another character push back on the shift, or have Tamsin explicitly concede: 'I said I wanted a number. I was wrong to ask for one — here's why a floor is the only honest answer.'

findings.Quote: the fixed cold-edge that took the warmth and gave nothing back
findings.Note: purple abstraction standing in for concrete sensory detail; fails literal scrutiny as an image of a room
findings.Fix: replace with a specific physical detail of the room she remembers

findings.Quote: the two kinds of knowing collapsing into each other, exactly the thing she'd sworn to keep apart
findings.Note: Explicitly names the thematic mechanism set up in the prior beat, telling the reader the significance instead of trusting the enacted scene (drone, reversal, override) to demonstrate it.
findings.Fix: Cut the explanatory clause; let the reversal and override stand as the collapse without labeling it.

findings.Quote: Celeste shook her head. A small motion, one she'd clearly made to herself before. "Jace is allowed to be afraid for me."
findings.Note: This response is attributed to Celeste but answers a question posed by Celeste herself to Tamsin, and the attribution tag jars against the surrounding dialogue exchange between Celeste and Tamsin — it reads as if Celeste is answering her own rhetorical question rather than the entity/Jace doing so, breaking the confrontation's logic.
findings.Fix: Attribute the line to Jace/the entity's voice, or clarify it's Celeste quoting what Jace said, e.g. 'Jace says he's allowed to be afraid for me.'

findings.Quote: The one route that left no trace had been paved over by the people he was trying to avoid, and now the only unmonitored path was the one he'd just spent walking into the open.
findings.Fix: clarify what the remaining unmonitored path actually is, since the passage asserts both that the trace-free route is gone and that an unmonitored path still exists without identifying it

findings.Quote: "I know." Aleksei picked up the folded document and held it a moment.
findings.Note: Rennick's line 'I know' answers a request Aleksei has not yet made explicit in this exchange — the dialogue skips the actual ask, making the response a non sequitur
findings.Fix: restore Aleksei's request line before Rennick's 'I know' response

findings.Quote: He had the stillness of a man who'd spent a decade with no Network signal and learned that stillness was its own cover.
findings.Note: Tells us the meaning of the stillness rather than showing it, and doubles down with an abstract aphorism about cover.
findings.Fix: Cut the explanatory clause; let the stillness itself carry the point without the essayistic gloss.

findings.Quote: like a ceiling dropping
findings.Note: stock disaster-image shorthand for sudden overwhelm, undercuts the procedural specificity built up around the read
findings.Fix: replace with an image specific to her sensory vocabulary (pressure/temperature/direction) rather than a generic collapse metaphor

findings.Quote: Her ears had already moved on, scanning the room, but her eyes stayed.
findings.Note: This directly conflicts with the beat's opening claim that her ears 'snapped toward Analog' and stayed fixed as a threat-detection lock in ref 1, and undercuts the standoff tension by having her attention immediately fragment.
findings.Fix: Keep ears locked on Analog to maintain the standoff: 'Her ears stayed on him too, tracking.'

findings.Quote: They'd even left the book face-down — because they knew which way she'd lay it when she finished reading.
findings.Note: logically odd: a book left face-down before she's arrived can't reflect how *she* would leave it after reading — this is inferring a habit not yet observed in this scenario, undercutting the intended chill
findings.Fix: clarify it mirrors an established habit of hers the planner already knew (e.g., 'the way she always left hers') rather than presenting it as a predictive flourish

findings.Quote: I want you to know I've accounted for that.
findings.Note: The purpose calls for a self-reckoning as emotional close, but 'accounted for' is vague corporate-speak that dodges rather than delivers reckoning, undercutting the payoff.
findings.Fix: Have her name a concrete cost or action, even obliquely, so the reckoning lands rather than gestures.

findings.Quote: a name held at the end of a life wasn't a word so much as a direction with a person at the end of it
findings.Note: abstract, aphoristic phrasing that tells rather than shows the emotional payload of the moment
findings.Fix: ground it in a concrete sensory beat instead of a definitional statement

findings.Quote: You couldn't undo eight months of grief in eight minutes.
findings.Note: Filler-wit aphorism stating the obvious math already conveyed by the scene, reads as a universal-truth quip rather than character thought.
findings.Fix: Cut the sentence; let the number stand on its own.

findings.Quote: That was the part Tamsin couldn't get a flat edge under.
findings.Note: strained, unclear metaphor — 'flat edge under' doesn't parse literally and reads as reaching for profundity
findings.Fix: replace with a clearer statement of her inability to reconcile the kindness with the predation

findings.Quote: a thing he did with evidence bags, with photographs, with anything he needed to sit square before he could think past it
findings.Note: Tells the reader the meaning of the gesture instead of trusting the action itself; explanatory aside undercuts the show-don't-tell effect.
findings.Fix: Cut the explanatory clause and let the gesture stand alone, or show it once earlier so this callback lands without narration.

findings.Quote: That meant it pushed and didn't pull. Whatever left a person in that room went out into the signal field, and the field couldn't reach back in to stop it. It ran one direction only. Nothing connected to the Network could interrupt it.
findings.Note: redundant restatement of the same fact four times in a row reads as padding rather than escalating technical detail, weakening the 'technical profile' purpose
findings.Fix: cut repetition to two statements max: the mechanism and its consequence

findings.Quote: It had stayed in the room after Sol died, the way a smell stays.
findings.Note: Stock simile that undersells the uncanny threat with a mundane, slightly comic comparison.
findings.Fix: Replace with an image consistent with the entity's established sensory signature (cold, attention, drain) rather than a domestic smell simile.

findings.Quote: The more the man was worth to the case, the more danger he was in. The two climbed together.
findings.Note: Stated as a flat aphorism/universal truth rather than dramatized tension; tells the reader the stakes instead of showing them through specific detail.
findings.Fix: Fold the danger into a concrete detail — e.g., what escalation the man's usefulness would actually trigger inside the operation.

findings.Quote: He didn't show up in the substrate at all. He was the gap the signal flowed around.
findings.Note: directly undercut two paragraphs later when the Tributary demonstrates it can track and respond to him specifically (killing his breaker attempt, running around his interrupt) — if it truly can't model him, it shouldn't be able to counter his actions in real time
findings.Fix: clarify that it can react to his physical interference without 'seeing' him as a person/pattern, to preserve the gap-in-substrate logic

findings.Quote: Twenty-three months of clean anonymity
findings.Note: The record says twenty-three months of anonymous intake for Burokas in this beat, but the receipt sent in the next beat references 'Your intake of 14 months ago' — the two numbers describing the same relationship don't reconcile.
findings.Fix: Align the timeframes — either both should reference the same duration, or clarify that 14 months refers to a specific intake event within the 23-month pattern.

findings.Quote: Something that had been waiting months for a body to speak into found one, and it did not want to pass out and away — it wanted to stay, to sink deeper
findings.Note: Overwritten personification tells us the threat rather than showing a concrete sensory beat; abstract 'wanted to stay/sink deeper' is vague menace-filler.
findings.Fix: Ground it in one physical, specific detail (a smell, a sound, a memory-flash) instead of naming the entity's desires abstractly.

findings.Quote: The lights along the north corridor cut out one bank at a time, counting down the hundred and thirty feet, and Voss heard the refrigeration unit's lock disengage.
